From: Sam Holt <sam.holt@atlasbank.com>

Subject: Request: cross-region failover SLA / RTO & RPO carveout

Hi Chloe + Lauren,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday. We ran the internal resilience team debrief this morning and have a follow-up ask around multi-region failover commitments. Our compliance group requires explicit RTO/RPO targets for cross-region failover; the standard 99.99% uptime commitment is fine for normal operations, but for regulatory reporting we need defined behavior for a regional outage that causes a full switchover.

Specifically, AtlasBank would like Redwood to consider an addendum that:
- Commits to a measured cross-region failover RTO of no more than 30 minutes for core inference routes (auth, request routing, and model serving for payment scoring).
- Commits to an RPO of no greater than 1 hour (we understand caching and KV semantics can vary).
- Defines responsibilities for warm-standby capacity (who owns reserved capacity during standby?) and a test cadence for failover drills (quarterly preferred).

If a 30/1 target is not feasible for hosted Shared plans, we'd like to discuss a carveout that describes guaranteed time-to-restore for a Dedicated/Private footprint. Can you share a proposed contractual addendum and any technical constraints we should be aware of (e.g., replication lag, snapshot frequency, KMS cross-region key policy)?

Attached is our Resilience Questionnaire (redacted).

Appreciate a quick turn on this — our security/compliance team will need language for the procurement packet by next week.

Best,
Sam
Senior Resilience Engineer
Atlas Bank

Sam — appreciate the specificity. We typically treat multi-region DR differently depending on deployment mode: Hosted Shared, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). High level: 
- Hosted Shared: standard uptime SLA (99.99%) with best-effort cross-region failover; we do not commit to <1-hour RTO for individual customers on this tier.
- Dedicated: we can contract stronger RTO/RPO targets if the customer takes reserved standby capacity or a dedicated warm standby pool.
- Private: contractual SLAs remain negotiable with on-prem commitments and network/ops integration.

Proposal (to expedite procurement):
- Draft an addendum for AtlasBank that commits to 99.95% availability for cross-region failover of specified critical routes with a target RTO of 60 minutes and RPO of 1 hour for Dedicated deployments by default.
- Offer an accelerated option (RTO 30 minutes) if AtlasBank commits to a dedicated standby pool sized at X vGPUs and agrees to quarterly DR drills and a monthly warm-standby billing minimum.
- Include operational requirements: quarterly failover tests, documented rollback plan, scoped region pairs, and a defined incident commander contact list.

I'm attaching an initial addendum draft (commercial language + technical appendix) — Chloe/Marcus, please review the technical viability and mark any must-haves we cannot contractually promise. Sam, if that structure looks acceptable I can produce a version with bill-of-materials and cost delta.

—Lauren

Subject: RE: Request: cross-region failover SLA / RTO & RPO carveout

Hi all — Marcus from infra. TL;DR: we can support a bounded carveout but with constraints and operational preconditions.

Technical summary:
- For Dedicated pools with pre-provisioned warm standby, we can guarantee an RTO of 30 minutes for control-plane failover (routing, auth) assuming the following: latest VM images, pre-synchronized model artifacts, and a verified cold-start optimization profile. Model weight transfer and quantized artifact sync must be done continuously; worst-case time budget: 14 minutes for container/pod warmup, 8 minutes for KV cache population via incremental snapshot apply, 8 minutes for routing reconfiguration — leaves ~0-10 minutes buffer.
- For data-plane/stateful models: RPO of 1 hour is achievable iff Atlas enables cross-region object replication with a minimum snapshot frequency of 15 minutes and allows cross-region KMS wrapping (we can support Bring-Your-Own-Key with replicated key policy).
- For Hosted Shared tenants we cannot guarantee any per-customer cross-region RTO/RPO given multi-tenant capacity constraints.

Operational preconditions to be codified in the addendum:
1) Dedicated warm-standby sizing and a monthly minimum commitment (size to be agreed after an architecture review).
2) Quarterly failover drills with documented tickets and runbook signoff; Atlas must participate in post-drill RCA and remediation scheduling.
3) Cross-region KMS policy allowing key unwrap in standby region or an approved key-rotation exception during recovery.
4) A defined SLA credit structure tied specifically to the cross-region activation window.

We can produce a Technical Appendix that lists exact artifact sync steps, monitoring signals used to trigger automated failover, and the rollback gating checks. If Atlas agrees to dedicate capacity and KMS allowances, I can commit to 30m/1h for the in-scope routes; otherwise we should default to conservative 60m/1h.

—Marcus Lin
